links.outcome: Proportion of ChatGPT-using students who used it to help write clinical notes
links.effect: 21.0% (33/157) of ChatGPT users reported using it to help write clinical notes, and 46.5% (73/157) used it for assignments; the authors flag patient confidentiality concerns.
links.quote: Notably, 21.0% (33/157) of participants responded having used ChatGPT to help write clinical notes.

links.outcome: Association between baseline AI understanding and cross-checking or editing of ChatGPT output
links.effect: Moderate or advanced AI understanding was associated with cross-checking (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.08-4.97) and editing (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.05-5.71) versus basic or limited understanding.
links.quote: Students who reported moderate or advanced baseline understanding of AI were more likely to practice conscientious use habits, such as cross-checking (odds ratio [OR] 2.31, 95% CI 1.08-4.97) and editing (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.05-5.71) ChatGPT output before using it, than those who reported a basic or limited understanding.

unlisted_practices: Structured AI education in medical school curricula for students

screen.reason: National cross-sectional survey examining medical students' actual use, habits (such as cross-checking and clinical note writing), and perceptions of ChatGPT in education and clinical training.
